sundarikabhāradvāja.notes: SN 7.9 and Snp 3.4 name the brahmin offering a fire sacrifice beside the Sundarikā. SN 7.8 concerns Aggika Bhāradvāja at Rājagaha. The entry places the MN 7 meeting on the Bāhukā, but MN 7:1.2 sets it in Jeta’s Grove, and at 19.3 the brahmin asks whether Gotama goes to the river to bathe. SN 7.10:18.5 recalls SN 7.9 in the chapter recap.

sundarikā.notes: MN 7 names the river among the bathing places. SN 7.9 and Snp 3.4 explicitly place the sacrifice on its bank in Kosala. The page matches also pick up SN 7.8 at Rājagaha and Snp 3.3 in Jeta’s Grove.

sundarī.notes: Thig 13.4:24.1–25.4 identifies the Buddha’s liberated disciple from Varanasi. Her biography is missing. Entry 03 describes the female wanderer killed in Ud 4.8, also named in the Ud 4.10 recap and the Dhp 306 story heading. Keep her out of the nun’s dictionary line. Ud 4.8:4.3 says the wanderers killed her and put her body in a ditch. The hired killers and heap of rubbish are details from the entry’s expanded account. The word sundari at Snp 3.12:65.2 recalls the discourse on Sundarika Bhāradvāja, Snp 3.4.

sundarīnandā.notes: Thig 5.4 signs the verses Sundarīnandā therī. The entry’s Thag.vs.82–6 should refer to Therīgāthā verses 82–86. Thag 1.82 belongs to Kassapa. AN 1.240 names the foremost nun in meditation as Nandā, accounting for the shorter name there and the page overlap with the adjacent AN groups.

sunetta.notes: AN 7.66:13–14 recounts Sunetta’s cultivation of love and explains why he was still subject to rebirth. AN 7.73 also names the teacher. The packet misses the joined form sunettaarakena in the recap at AN 7.74:12.4.

sunimmita.notes: AN 8.36:8.3 identifies Sunimmita among the gods who delight in creation. SN 40.11:4.1 names the same godling. AN 8.37 concerns gifts and SN 40.10 concerns Sakka.

sunāga.notes: Thag 1.85 attributes the verse to Sunāga Thera. Thag 1.90:2.3 repeats his name in the list of elders for that chapter.

supassa.notes: The page reference has no mapped sutta. SN 15.20:4.1–5 gives all three identifying details together, the former name of Vepulla, the Suppiya people and the time of Kassapa Buddha.

suppabuddha.notes: Ud 5.3 names the leper of Rājagaha, also named in the Dhp 66 story heading. DN 14:1.12.7 names Vessabhū’s father Suppatita. It supplies no son named Suppabuddha. The other citation for entry 03 is to the Buddhavaṁsa, outside the app’s books.

suppiya.notes: DN 1 names the wanderer traveling with his pupil Brahmadatta. Thag 1.32 signs its verse Suppiyo thero. At Thag 1.40:2.1 Suppiya appears in the chapter’s roster of elders, after Vaḍḍhamāna’s own verse. AN 1.264 and AN 8.91–117 explicitly name the laywoman Suppiyā. SN 15.20 names the Suppiya people.

suppiyā.notes: SN 15.20:4.2–5 names the people who climbed Mount Supassa in Kassapa’s time, despite the unmapped page citation. AN 1.264 names the laywoman foremost in caring for the sick, and AN 8.91–117 calls her suppiyā upāsikā. The surrounding AN 1 groups and AN 8.118–119 are page overlaps.

suriya.notes: SN 2.10:1.2 calls him sūriyo devaputto, translated ‘the Sun God’. The long-ū form has its own DPD sense, sūriya 2, and the packet finds no mentions. DN 20:14.5–6 places him at the head of the sun gods. Correct the entry’s account of SN 2.10:6.1, where Rāhu releases Sūriya and goes trembling to Vepacitti. The entry gives those last actions to Suriya. SN 2.11 concerns Candimasa. DN 32 describes the sun’s disk without giving the fifty-league measurement.

susīma.notes: Sakka sends the godling against the asuras in SN 11.2. SN 11.1 gives the parallel episode for Suvīra. SN 12.70 names the wanderer who seeks ordination from Ānanda, under DPD’s short-i spelling susima 2. The packet omits that discourse, and SN 12.69 is a page overlap. SN 2.29 has another short-i godling who praises Sāriputta. DPPN treats his identity with entry 05 as tentative. SN 2.30 and SN 11.10 recall the respective deities in their chapter lists.

sutanu.notes: SN 52.3:1.1 places Anuruddha on the bank of the Sutanu near Sāvatthī. DPD treats sutanutīre as a compound. The packet also misses the bare sutanu in the recap at SN 52.10:3.2. SN 52.2 gives only Sāvatthī.

sutanā.notes: AN 8.91–117 names Sutanā in the list of laywomen with Bojjhā. AN 8.89 and AN 8.90 are adjacent page matches.

suvīra.notes: SN 11.1 names the godling Sakka orders to march against the asuras. SN 11.10:7.1 lists Suvīra and Susīma as separate titles in the chapter recap.

suyāma.notes: All three listed passages call Suyāma a devaputta. Thag 1.74:1.5 signs the verse Suyāmano thero, the variant given in entry 04. Thag 1.80:2.3 recalls him under the same spelling. DPD gives the monk his own headword suyāmana, so neither occurrence is available for a sutta assignment here.

sādhuka.notes: SN 55.6:1.4 places Isidatta and Purāṇa in Sādhuka. SN 55.5 is an adjacent conversation with Sāriputta.

sāgata.notes: AN 1.232 names Sāgata foremost in skill with the fire element. The page also picks up AN 1.235–247 and AN 1.248–257.

sāketa.notes: DN 16:5.17.4 lists the city, and MN 24 gives the journey there from Sāvatthī. The named settings are in AN 4.24, AN 5.144, SN 2.18 and SN 47.26. AN 4.23, AN 5.143, SN 2.17, SN 2.19 and SN 47.24–25 are page overlaps. SN 52.5 and SN 52.6 each open with the compound Sāketanidānaṁ.

sālha.notes: AN 3.66:1.3 calls Nandaka’s visitor migāranattā. DPD points to AN 3.67 and its gloss spells Visākha where DPPN explains the relationship through Visākhā Migāramātā. AN 4.196 calls Sāḷha and his companion Abhaya Licchavis. AN 3.70 and AN 4.200 give bare discourse titles in chapter recaps. DN 16:2.6–7 and SN 55.8 identify the deceased monk at Ñātika. The mapped AN 3.65, AN 4.195, DN 17 and SN 55.7 miss the corresponding episodes.

sālā.notes: MN 41 and MN 60 both name the Kosalan brahmin village in their opening. The citation list omits MN 60 even though the entry cites the Apaṇṇakasutta. SN 47.4 and SN 48.51 also give the village as their setting, with the titles recalled in SN 47.10 and SN 48.60.

sāmagāma.notes: MN 104 places the Buddha at Sāmagāma, and DN 29:2.1 places Cunda’s visit to Ānanda there. AN 6.21:1.1 gives the lotus pond and uses the separate DPD form sāmagāmake. MN 103 is the adjacent page match.

sāmaṇḍaka.notes: SN 39.1–15 names the wanderer questioning Sāriputta at Ukkacelā. SN 38.16 belongs to Jambukhādaka’s collection. AN 10.65 and 10.66 give the Nālakagāma conversations under the separate DPD headword sāmaṇḍakāni. SN 44.11:5.3 is a recap of the collections.

sāmāvatī.notes: The same biography describes Udena’s queen and the laywoman foremost in loving-kindness at AN 1.261. AN 1.248–257 and 1.268–277 are page overlaps. Ud 7.10:1.3 names her as head of the women who died in the palace fire, in the compound sāmāvatīpamukhāni. The Dhp 21 story heading also carries her name.
